what_it_does: Dataflow circuits are a style of digital hardware design where computation is triggered by the arrival of data tokens rather than a central clock — useful in high-level synthesis (HLS), the process of automatically generating chip logic from a high-level program description. Optimizing such circuits by simplifying their structure (removing redundant buffers, merging operations) requires proving that the rewritten circuit does exactly the same thing as the original. The problem is that classical equivalence-checking techniques assume a fixed-clock sequential circuit; dataflow circuits can handle tokens arriving in any order and at varying rates, which breaks those assumptions. ElasticMiter builds a verification framework specifically for this style: it constructs a combined comparison circuit (a miter) that would flag any input sequence where the two versions diverge, then proves no such sequence exists. Every simplification rule in the optimization system is verified this way before use, giving a mathematically guaranteed-correct rewriting toolchain.
